chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Muhammad ibn Isa from Yunus from Muhammad ibn Muqarrin ibn Abdullah ibn Zama'a ibn Subay from his father from his grandfather from the grandfather of his father that, the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) wrote to him in his letter which he wrote to him in his own handwriting when he sent him regarding the alms-tax (Zakat):

Whoever upon whom the charity of the jadha' (four-year-old camel) falls, and he does not have a jadha' but has a hiqqah (three-year-old camel), then the hiqqah is accepted from him, and two sheep or twenty dirhams are added with it.
And whoever upon whom the charity of the hiqqah falls, and he does not have a hiqqah but has a jadha', then the jadha' is accepted from him, and the collector gives him two sheep or twenty dirhams.

And whoever upon whom the charity of a hiqqah falls, and he does not have a hiqqah but has a ibnath labun (two-year-old camel), then the ibnath labun is accepted from him, and he gives with it two sheep or twenty dirhams.

And whoever upon whom the charity of an ibnath labun falls, and he does not have an ibnath labun but has a hiqqah, then the hiqqah is accepted from him, and the collector gives him two sheep or twenty dirhams.

And whoever upon whom the charity of an ibnath labun falls, and he does not have an ibnath labun but has an ibnath makhadh (one-year-old camel), then the ibnath makhadh is accepted from him, and he gives with it two sheep or twenty dirhams.

And whoever upon whom the charity of an ibnath makhadh falls, and he does not have an ibnath makhadh but has an ibnath labun, then the ibnath labun is accepted from him, and the collector gives him two sheep or twenty dirhams.
And whoever does not have an ibnath makhadh in its proper state, but has a male ibnath labun, then the male ibnath labun is accepted from him, and there is nothing added with it.

And whoever has nothing with him except four camels, and he has no wealth other than them, then there is nothing in them unless its owner wishes. So when his wealth reaches five camels, then there is a sheep in them.

key_terms.شَاةٌ: A sheep (used as compensation or Zakat)
key_terms.صَدَقَةُ الْجَذَعَةِ: The alms-tax due on a four-year-old female camel

ai.seo_question: What are the rules for Zakat substitution when the required age of camel is not available?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through a strong chain to Imam Ali (AS), outlines the practical jurisprudence of Zakat substitution (badal), ensuring that the obligation is fulfilled even if the exact age category of the camel is unavailable. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on ease and fairness, allowing for compensation of two sheep or twenty dirhams to balance the value difference between age groups. The text also clarifies the exemption for small herds of four camels and the acceptance of male camels without penalty, demonstrating the flexibility in applying fixed legal rulings to real-world scenarios.
